text.p: President Fidel Ramos said on Monday corruption in the government had become such a nightmare that Filipinos believed their officials were rich because they had stolen public money.

He said the people had become so sceptical about their officials that accusations of corruption were accepted as fact not because the charges were credible "but because graft in the government has become accepted as a commonplace malady."
Ramos spoke at the groundbreaking ceremony for a new building for a special court to try cases of corrupt officials.
Officials estimate the government has lost $48 billion in potential income due to corruption during the past 20 years.

Such has public cynicism grown that "government transactions are almost always believed to be dishonest, government officials are almost always believed to be rich with ill-gotten wealth," Ramos told judges and prosecutors.
Worse, he added, "the not-so-crooked government officials decide they may as well be crooked because they feel everybody else is doing it and getting away with it."
"The nightmare of corruption in public service is one of the most persistent afflictions of our country," Ramos said.
He referred to a recent international study which listed the Philippines as the sixth most corrupt country in the world a few years ago but now rated it as the 11th, improving its image.
"This is no cause for jubilation. For me it is both embarrassing and challenging," he said.

Ramos urged state prosecutors to intensify their pursuit of corrupt officials and said Filipinos on the whole "must demonstrate that each of us should be so ashamed of graft that we will not keep company with grafters."
